newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ investment returns improve in Sept qtr -survey.
newsitem.headline: NZ investment returns improve in Sept qtr -survey.

text.p: New Zealand investment returns in the September quarter were the best for the year despite, or perhaps because of, the October 12 general election, Mercer Investment Consulting said on Tuesday.
The median return before tax and expenses was 3.7 percent compared with 0.6 percent in the June quarter and 1.9 percent in the March quarter.
Domestic assets performed best, with the NZSE-40 returning 5.8 percent for the quarter and the smaller companies index performing even better with a 7.0 percent return.
The domestic bond market rose 5.1 percent while the Salomon Brothers World Government Bond Index returned 4.5 percent (hedged to the NZ dollar).
The New Zealand property index returned 4.9 percent in the quarter, rising 12.8 percent over the year.
The poorest performing class was overseas equities where the MSCI World Accumulation Index fell 0.7 percent in New Zealand dollar terms.
The best fund manager for the quarter was Prudential, with a 4.8 percent return, followed by ANZ with 4.6 percent, Armstrong Jones with 4.5 percent and Bankers Trust with 4.2 percent.
The lowest return by far was Westpac's 1.5 percent followed by Colonial on 2.3 percent, AMP on 2.7 percent and Citibank on 3.0 percent.
There was a shift during the quarter out of cash into bonds and shares.

However, three of the top four performing funds had increased their cash holdings by quarter end. The largest increase came from BT which has since then significantly reduced its exposure to cash in favour of domestic equities. Westpac on the other hand has continued to maintain its high exposure to cash.
